original_source_text: Panmnesia's official article identifies the exact ISCA paper and describes a next-stage CXL controller with shared buffers across physical, link, and transaction layers to reduce synchronization overhead. It describes a fabric switch supporting port-based routing alongside hierarchy-based routing, larger memory expansion at similar latency, improved system bandwidth, and stable performance with as many as 64 nodes. The article also distinguishes product and pre-release silicon context from the paper evaluation.

record_under_review.evidence_span: Panmnesia's official ISCA announcement describes a CXL controller that shares buffers across physical, link, and transaction layers to reduce layer-level synchronization overhead, plus a fabric switch supporting port-based routing alongside hierarchy-based routing. The announcement says the design expands memory connectivity while keeping latency in a similar range, improves total bandwidth, and shows stable performance with as many as 64 nodes. It also identifies pre-release PCIe 6.4-CXL 3.2 switch silicon and PCIe 7.0-CXL 4.0 controller IP as productization context.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Silicon-proven CXL controller and switch, with PCIe/CXL physical interfaces, shared layer buffers, and port-based routing; exact process node, latency, bandwidth, power, and test configuration require the paper.
record_under_review.limits: The source is an official company announcement, not the captured IEEE paper. It is subject to author/company framing and omits detailed latency distributions, bandwidth numbers, power, area, process, workloads, and independent reproduction.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: A unified CXL controller with shared cross-layer buffers and a port-based-routing fabric switch that supports flexible topologies while retaining hierarchy-based routing compatibility.
metrics: stable performance with as many as 64 nodes
similar latency range while expanding memory connectivity
silicon-proven implementation and pre-release product context
record_under_review.problem: Early CXL designs inherited PCIe-oriented layer separation and hierarchical connectivity, creating synchronization overhead and limiting the scale of memory-centric fabrics.
record_under_review.title: A Silicon-Proven Unified Low-Latency CXL Controller and Port-Based Routing Switch for Memory-Centric Fabrics
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Memory-centric CXL fabric scaling and multi-node connectivity; the company announcement reports stable performance with up to 64 nodes but does not expose the full paper’s workload matrix.
